en_summary: @jasonfurman argues it is a fallacy that higher rates hurt supply side solutions: rate hikes reduce much more demand before any supply, e.g. cutting $100 of upfront spending versus $5 a year less supply 3 years later, which is disinflationary.
ko_summary: @jasonfurman은 금리 인상이 공급 측 해결책을 해친다는 건 오류라고 했다. 금리 인상은 공급보다 수요를 훨씬 먼저, 더 많이 줄인다. 예컨대 선행 지출 100달러를 줄이고 3년 뒤 공급은 연 5달러만 줄어 물가를 낮춘다.
text:
John, you are almost always an admirably clear thinker. But you endorse a common fallacy when you make this argument: "Higher rates hurt supply-side solutions in housing, energy, autos, and other capital intensive industries"

The issue is that much more demand is reduced before any supply is reduced. For example, higher interest rates might cut $100 of upfront spending and result in $5/yr less in supply starting 3 years from now. That is deflationary.

You can also think of your argument in reverse. If the government made a big increase in infrastructure investment or businesses suddenly decided to invest more in autos we would expect that to put upward pressure on inflation not downward pressure.

zh_summary: 企業級SSD收入在第二季達到約380億美元，因為AI代理需要更多快速儲存以處理不斷增長的上下文，使SSD成為AI基礎設施的重要部分。$SNDK季度收入增長103%之所以有趣，是因為其企業級SSD市佔率僅約8%，相較整體NAND的11%，仍有追趕空間。$MU已處於領先地位，企業級SSD市佔率約19%，相較NAND的15%，數據中心SSD現已佔其NAND收入超過三分之二，因為AI推動了更豐富的儲存組合。
en_summary: Enterprise SSD revenue reached ~$38B in Q2 as AI agents need more fast storage to handle growing context, making SSDs an important part of AI infrastructure. $SNDK's 103% QoQ revenue jump is interesting because it holds only ~8% of enterprise SSDs versus 11% of overall NAND, leaving room to catch up. $MU is further ahead with ~19% enterprise SSD share versus 15% of NAND, and data center SSDs now account for over 2/3 of its NAND revenue as AI drives a richer storage mix.
ko_summary: 기업용 SSD 매출은 2분기에 약 380억 달러에 달했는데, AI 에이전트가 증가하는 컨텍스트를 처리하기 위해 더 많은 빠른 스토리지를 필요로 하기 때문이며, SSD는 AI 인프라의 중요한 부분이 되고 있다. $SNDK의 103% 분기 대비 매출 성장이 흥미로운 이유는 기업용 SSD 점유율이 전체 NAND의 11% 대비 약 8%에 불과해 따라잡을 여지가 있기 때문이다. $MU는 기업용 SSD 점유율 약 19%로 NAND 15% 대비 앞서 있으며, 데이터센터 SSD가 이제 NAND 매출의 3분의 2 이상을 차지하는데, AI가 더 풍부한 스토리지 믹스를 주도하기 때문이다.
text:
Enterprise SSD revenue reached ~$38B in Q2 as AI agents need more fast storage to handle growing context making SSDs a really important part of AI infrastructure.

That also helps explain why $SNDK 103% QoQ revenue jump is so interesting because it still holds only ~8% of enterprise SSDs versus 11% of overall NAND leaving plenty of room to catch up.

$MU is already further ahead with ~19% enterprise SSD share versus 15% of NAND and data center SSDs now account for over 2/3 of its NAND revenue as AI drives a richer storage mix.

name: John_Hempton
zh_summary: 這是對金融機構如何破產的驚人誤解。它們破產不是因為資產變壞，而是因為融資變得不可能。當然，當融資市場不再信任資產時，融資就會變壞。它們可以盡可能延長和假裝。但如果資產支持票據市場不信任資產，這就幫不了它們。在這種情況下，信任消失的可能性非常高。
en_summary: This is a spectacular misunderstanding of how financial institutions go bankrupt. They go bankrupt not when the assets go bad but when their funding becomes impossible. Sure the funding goes bad when the funding market no longer trusts the assets. They can extend and pretend as long as they like. But it won't help them if say the asset backed paper market doesn't trust the assets. In this case there is a very high chance that trust has gone away.
ko_summary: 이것은 금융 기관이 어떻게 파산하는지에 대한 놀라운 오해다. 자산이 나빠질 때가 아니라 자금 조달이 불가능해질 때 파산한다. 물론 자금 시장이 더 이상 자산을 신뢰하지 않을 때 자금 조달이 나빠진다. 그들은 원하는 만큼 연장하고 가장할 수 있다. 하지만 자산 담보 어음 시장이 자산을 신뢰하지 않으면 도움이 되지 않는다. 이 경우 신뢰가 사라진 가능성이 매우 높다.

They go bankrupt not when the assets go bad but when their funding becomes impossible.

Sure the funding goes bad when the funding market no longer trusts the assets.

In this case there is a very high chance that trust has gone away.

name: Tobias Carlisle
zh_summary: @Greenbackd：優質債券只能防範某一類崩盤。在最近兩個截然不同的壓力年份，各類股票均下跌，國際股票及房地產在兩次崩盤中都未能保護美國投資者。
en_summary: @Greenbackd: high quality bonds protect against one kind of crash but not another. In the two recent stress years, stocks of every kind fell, and international stocks and real estate did not protect US investors in either.
ko_summary: @Greenbackd: 우량 채권은 한 종류의 폭락만 막는다. 최근 두 번의 스트레스 해에 모든 주식이 하락했고 해외 주식과 부동산은 어느 쪽에서도 미국 투자자를 보호하지 못했다.
text:
If high-quality bonds protect against one kind of crash but not the other, what else belongs in the portfolio? Many products are sold as crash protection. The fairest test is to see what each did in the two most recent, very different stress years.

The chart repays careful reading.

* Stocks of every kind fell in both years. International stocks and real estate did not protect U.S. investors in either crash. Their case rests on long-run diversification, not crash protection. Within U.S. stocks, value shares held up far better than growth shares in 2022, but not in 2008.

* Long-term Treasuries and commodities are mirror images. Each saved the portfolio in one year and hurt it badly in the other. Holding a modest amount of both is a hedge against not knowing which engine will run.

* Gold roughly held its value in both years. It pays no income, and it can fall sharply in other periods, as it did in the early 1980s and in 2013. It is a store of value in a crisis, not a growth engine. 

*Managed futures gained in both years. These funds follow price trends across stocks, bonds, currencies, and commodities, going long or short. They tend to do well in extended declines of any kind. They can also lag for years in calm, trendless markets, and their fees are higher than index funds’.

*Treasury bills gained in both years. Its cost is low returns in good times.

Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said investors trade more on what they think the Fed will do than on what it should do, a view that sits uneasily with Kevin Warsh's push to say less about the outlook in pursuit of a purer market signal. 

"Having been on the market side of things for three decades, I think that what markets are looking for is they're looking for any guidance as to where the Fed is going to go. I know that bankers, investment professionals, their number one goal is to produce returns for themselves and their clients. That's their goal, that's the job. And to do that, they both want to look at what the fundamentals of the economy are doing and what they're saying, but I think they respond more based on what they think the Fed will do rather than what they think we should do. And so I think that it's important to take signal back from the markets about how the economy is progressing, but I take more signal about how the economy is progressing from the data, from the stories I hear in the district."

text:

Brent fell 1.5% to $105 as Saudi Arabia intercepted Houthi missiles and President Trump threatened to get involved on Saudi Arabia’s behalf.  The 10-year treasury yield eased 5.0bp to 5.19%. Banks kick off Q3 earnings today followed by tech heavyweights $ASML and $TSM later this week.  Sept CPI is due tomorrow, and Fed Chair Kevin Warsh speaks on Friday at an IMF-World Bank event. 

S&P 2026 EPS estimates of $367 continue to rise (+32% YoY) and imply a 21.3x P/E and 4.7% yield, remaining  inverted versus Treasuries, a rare setup outside the late-1990s dot-com bubble. Treasury yields are expected to retreat as the Iran conflict ends. I remain cautious on TSLA given its extended valuation, negative forward earnings revisions, and autonomous driving commoditization by competitors.

zh_summary: @aleabitoreddit 認為實體 AI 和人形機器人是 AI 的下一階段，$NVDA 在 CES 2025 的預測以及 Elon 對 $TSLA 十年內 10 億臺人形機器人的預言正在加速。宇樹執行長 8 月時認為機器人的「ChatGPT 時刻」最快需兩到三年，最長可達十年，測試 GPT-6 後現在預期 1 到 2 年內就會出現，定義為機器人能在 80% 的陌生環境中完成約 80% 的任務。他們引用一項機械手基準：碗任務中 Astra 20 次成功 19 次，Fable 5.1 為 8 次；拼圖任務兩者都只有 20 次中 2 次。
en_summary: @aleabitoreddit argues physical AI and humanoids are AI's next stage and the timeline for $NVDA's CES 2025 projections and Elon's 1 billion humanoids call for $TSLA is speeding up. Unitree's CEO, who in August saw a robotics "ChatGPT moment" taking two to three years or up to a decade, now expects it within 1 or 2 years after testing GPT-6, defined as robots doing about 80% of tasks in 80% of unfamiliar environments. They cite a hand benchmark where Astra placed the block in 19 of 20 trials vs Fable 5.1's 8 of 20, while both managed 2 of 20 on the puzzle task.
ko_summary: @aleabitoreddit는 피지컬 AI와 휴머노이드가 AI의 다음 단계이며, $NVDA의 CES 2025 전망과 Elon의 $TSLA 관련 10년 내 휴머노이드 10억 대 예측이 앞당겨지고 있다고 봅니다. Unitree CEO는 8월에는 로봇의 "ChatGPT 모먼트"까지 빠르면 2~3년, 길면 10년이 걸린다고 했지만 GPT-6을 테스트한 뒤 1~2년 안에 가능하다고 기대합니다. 그 기준은 낯선 환경의 80%에서 작업의 약 80%를 수행하는 것입니다. 로봇 손 벤치마크에서 Astra는 그릇 과제 20회 중 19회 성공해 Fable 5.1의 8회를 앞섰고, 퍼즐 과제는 둘 다 20회 중 2회였다고 인용했습니다.
text:
Physical AI + Humanoids are the next progression of AI.

$NVDA CES 2025 projections and Elon's prediction on $TSLA + 1 Billion humanoids in the next decade, seems to be speeding up. 

New statement from Unitree CEO after testing GPT-6 on their humanoid program was that:

- In August, before GPT-6's release, Wang said the industry could take two to three years at its fastest pace, or as long as a decade, to reach its "ChatGPT moment"

- Now, OpenAI's GPT-6 model prompted expectations that a breakthrough could happen "within 1 or 2 years"

- He defined that moment as robots being able to complete around 80 per cent of tasks in 80 per cent of unfamiliar environments using voice or text commands.

- "It's possible that, say, a GPT-7 model released next year could directly crack the problems of embodied intelligence"

- "The whole embodied intelligence industry has been shaken up after the release of GPT-6"

Just looking at some benchmarks on robotic hand manipulation, "On the bowl task Astra placed the block in 19 of 20 trials, against Fable 5.1's 8 of 20".

But for the puzzle task "Astra completed the insertion 2 times in 20 against Fable 5.1's 2 in 20"".. so we're getting there. 

But going from 2-3 years (potentially to a decade), and compressing that down to 1 or 2 years (to achieve 80%+ of tasks in unfamiliar environemnts) is a significant change in outlook.

text:
What oversupply? Even in the lower end ranges that they're focusing on, Chinese pluggable makers like Innolight are still bottlenecked for 70-100mW ranges from ECOC channel checks. 

Cambridge wouldn't be going out financing suppliers with convertible loans for scarce laser capacity. 

Suppliers wouldn't be raising ASPs if there was overcapacity. Also not all CW lasers are the same. China is a ways away from from scaling UHP lasers needed for CPO, which is why there's still premiums given to $LITE, $COHR, $SIVE. 

$LITE lasers are sold out into 2029 and they're starting negotiations into 2030. 

I don't think anyone genuinely believes that China will flood the laser markets medium term, even both $LITE /  $AAOI CEO said there was a difference between comments made and what they're actually seeing. 

From AOI on China: "of them, they are working maybe 70 mW or very few can really do 100 mW. For 300 mW laser, especially DWDM spec, we don't see that."

 "Not in the next two, three years, especially the demand is so big. Okay? Even combined AOI, Lumentum, Coherent, Broadcom all together, it's still very tough to meet the customer demand in the next few years"

From Lumentum last month: "At least at the moment, we see no impact from any Chinese laser supply."

But whenever markets want a correction people just blindly point to China with memory or optics while ignoring what's actually occurring with demand imbalances + LTAs spanning many years and constantly extending.
